title: Cyber harassment at the workplace - overlap with sexual harassment law
p1:
Can a sexually inappropriate WhatsApp message become workplace sexual harassment even if it was sent after office hours?

Surprisingly, yes. The fact that harassment happens outside the office or through a phone screen does not automatically take it outside workplace protection.
p2:
Many people assume sexual harassment law applies only to physical misconduct at the workplace. That's a misconception.

Under India's POSH Act, 2013, workplace-related harassment can extend to digital interactions, including sexually suggestive messages, inappropriate emails, unwanted video calls, explicit images and repeated personal advances through workplace communication channels.

The key question is not simply where the message was sent, but whether the conduct has a sufficient connection with the workplace and falls within the legal definition of sexual harassment.
p3:
For example, repeated sexually inappropriate messages from a senior colleague on WhatsApp may warrant a POSH complaint, even when sent late at night.

Practical takeaway: Preserve screenshots, emails, chat records and dates. Avoid deleting conversations that may establish a pattern of conduct. Report the incident to your organisation's Internal Committee (IC), where applicable.

Also remember: Not every instance of cyberbullying is sexual harassment under POSH. The nature of the conduct and its workplace connection matter.
conclusion: Should employers be legally accountable for sexually inappropriate messages sent through personal social media accounts when the people involved work together? Share your perspective.
